bio:
Martim Freitas Pereira is a British-Portuguese multidisciplinary graphic designer based in London, specialising in wayfinding, information and navigation-based, and exhibition design, with additional interests in immersive and editorial design.

His work is grounded in a thorough understanding of the nuances of designing for physical spaces and environments. With a sharp critical eye and keen attention to detail, Pereira approaches design with a broad perspective, placing emphasis on outcomes that are intentional and meaningful rather than surface-level.

A collaborative team player, he brings a fresh and unconventional perspective to his work.

projects.title: A-Z-DESIGN-BOOK-SERIF
projects.description:
A collective group project to create an A-Z visual book of key graphic design terms, including definitions and media examples. 

This project was completed with all of the Year 1 (’23-’24) Graphic Design course students.

I was specifically responsible for the definition and visual presentation of ‘serif’, exploring different examples of serif typefaces in logos, day-to-day life, historically, in different language scripts, and towards the future concept of serif.

projects.title: B33 Mini-zine
projects.description: A RISO-printed mini-zine about the B33 Chair.

projects.title: FACE Poster
projects.description:
This poster was created as a visual exercise - originally created from a simple shape and word, it was later developed into this finished poster design.

Whilst experimenting with creating different abstract shapes in Illustrator, I made a shape that I thought resembled a very abstract face, similar to the Easter Island heads or the Bafta trophy award.

I decided to build on this resemblance, creating a graphic that incorporated the word ‘FACE’ into its shape, which I later developed into this finished poster.

projects.title: GAME START
projects.description:
A board game titled 'GAME START', incorporating packaging design and functionality together as a response to a university brief in collaboration with Darcy Young & Jamie Bussey.

As part of this project, we had to explain our concept in a summative paragraph, as stated below:

"Our project combines packaging and a board game into one innovative, sustainable product. The box not only holds the game pieces but also unfolds into the game board itself, minimising waste and adding functionality.

"Using decorative touches like foiling and Litho printing, we created an attractive and fun design that draws players in and enhances the experience. 

"The packaging is designed to connect with others, allowing multiple boxes to combine into larger boards for expanded, exciting gameplay with friends and family. 

‍Inspired by the joy of connection, our product fosters meaningful relationships and friendly competition, creating cherished memories through shared play."

projects.title: reflections
projects.description: 'reflections' is a concept for an immersive experience based at St Dunstan in the East public garden, located in the City of London. This experience plays on the concept of water and reflection, utilising projection mapping, adaptive lighting, and surround audio to create a meditative and reflective experience to allow attendees to pause and reflect on themselves in a deep and calming environment.

projects.title: The North Greenwich Lines
projects.description: A ground-based wayfinding system concept, utilising physical floor trails and markers to help people navigate the Greenwich Peninsula.
